| D477 | **Moving in from Pipedrive (S7 of `docs/own-books-and-sales.md`), built in steps.** A store brings its CRM from Pipedrive by the account's API token: organisations to companies, persons to customers (D366's rules: no password, email not proven, nothing emailed, nobody subscribed), pipelines and stages, deals, activities and notes; a dry run first, then a count of what came and what did not. **Step 1, reading an account (built).** Pipedrive moved its lists to API v2 (`/api/v2/…`, cursor pages of at most 500; v1's are marked deprecated with a grace period of at least a year, and a third party gives 31 July 2026 for their end [U: Pipedrive's own date]), so organisations, persons, pipelines, stages, deals and activities are read from v2, and notes and the token's own user from v1, where they still are. `readPipedriveAccount()` (`src/server/pipedrive-client.ts`) sends the token in the `x-api-token` header (never in an address that could be logged), waits out a rate limit as `Retry-After` says (three times, at most a minute) and stops at its time budget; it only reads. `src/lib/pipedrive.ts` reads each record leniently into ours (a person's primary email and phone; a deal's value in its currency's minor units, none for a currency the platform does not keep; Pipedrive's activity types to a call, a meeting or a task, its own type kept; a note's HTML as text) and `planImport()` is the dry run: what would come over, and why the rest would not (a person without an email, a deal with nobody or no stage that comes over, an activity without a day or anyone, a note about no one). Tests: `pipedrive.test.ts`, `pipedrive-client.test.ts` (a stand-in API: pages by cursor and offset, the token only in the header, a rate limit waited out, a refused token, the budget). **Step 2, the import and its screen (built).** Settings → Moving in has a Pipedrive card while Deals is on (where Deals is offered but off, the one step before it): Homer pastes the API token (*Connect Pipedrive*: asked of Pipedrive whose it is, `/v1/users/me`, and kept encrypted in `commerce.crm_moves` with its Pipedrive company and shown by its last four), presses *See what comes over*, reads the counts and what is left out and why, and presses *Bring it over*; then *Open Deals*, and later *Bring over what's new*. A check and an import are one run (`PdRun`, `crm_moves.run`) going feed by feed (the team's users, organisations, persons, pipelines, stages, deals, activities, notes: each needing only what the ones before bring) and page by page within a budget, under a 90-second lease; each page is written and counted in one transaction, so a run that stops picks up at its page, and a page that cannot be written is tried again a few times before the run says so. The open page's ticks and the dispatcher's `pipedrive` job (40 seconds) move it on, so the owner may leave. Both follow the same rules (`skipOf()` in `src/lib/pipedrive.ts`; `planImport()` is a check of a whole account), so the check's counts are the import's. `commerce.crm_move_links` links each record brought over to its row here by Pipedrive company, kind and id: a second run brings only what is new and counts the rest as come before (what came over before is the store's now, never overwritten), and a row deleted here, or a person erased, keeps its link and is never brought back (the link holds only Pipedrive's number). What comes over: an organisation as a company (one of the same name adopted); a person with an email as a customer (D366: no password, not proven, nobody subscribed or emailed; someone the store has keeps what it has, only empty name and phone filled), a member of their organisation's company while it has room; pipelines (one of the same name adopted) and their stages; deals in their stage, with their value and currency (the store's when none), owner, close and reason (closed by a person); activities, due when Pipedrive says (its times are UTC; one without a time on its day in the store's zone), done or not, and marked told so the push job never reminds of them; notes, kept by a person's email: on their person, else their deal's, else someone of their (deal's) organisation, else left out. Deals and activities go to the team member with the Pipedrive user's email, else to nobody. *Disconnect* forgets the token and the run; what came over stays linked. Audited as `integration.pipedrive_connected`, `_disconnected`, `_import_started` and `_imported` with counts only. Tests: `pipedrive.test.ts` (a check page by page, what came before, where a note goes, owners by email), `pipedrive.int.test.ts` (against a database with a stand-in Pipedrive two records a page: a check writes nothing and counts what the import then brings; a second import brings nothing twice; a deleted deal stays deleted; a refused token). Kaizena Flow's own store (D467) has the same page. HubSpot after. Migration versions (applied by CI, 6 November 2026): `20261106185616_crm_moves`, `20261106185651_crm_moves_rules`. Advisors checked after: INFO only (RLS on, no policy, as every private table; the new index not yet used). Moving in's English words are fetched by its own screen (`admin-text-later.ts`), not with every admin page: the card's words had taken the home and /products past their script budgets. | 2026-11-06 | The owner's plan for leaving Pipedrive (S7): Human Web's sales data must come over before the pilot's exit. |
| D478 | **Our own ledger, in shadow (B2 of `docs/own-books-and-sales.md`), built in steps.** A double-entry journal kept by Kaizena Flow, run beside Tripletex for the pilot until three months agree to the øre on every account it posts to. **Step 1, the journal, its chart and its rules (built).** A book (`commerce.ledger_books`) is one legal entity's: its name and organisation number when it opened, its country (the pack: chart and VAT codes) and currency, its first day, a last day once closed, and the day it is locked through; one open book a store, so a change of the business behind the store (D473) closes one and opens the next and two entities' books never mix (Human Web AS's open on 1 January 2027 from the ENK's handover). Its chart (`ledger_accounts`) holds numbers that report as Skatteetaten's standard accounts (SAF-T's `StandardAccountID`, NS 4102's four digits, or a sub-account of one such as `19201` under 1920), each with its kind from its class and a default VAT code from the standard codes; both lists are Skatteetaten's published SAF-T files, read on 6 November 2026 and kept as they are (`src/data/ledger/no-saft.json`; low-rate output VAT is 2703, not 2702). A new Norwegian book starts with 38 accounts: all Kaizena Flow posts to and what a small business uses most. Entries (`ledger_entries`, `ledger_lines`) are written only by `commerce.ledger_post()`, which under the book's row lock refuses an entry that does not balance, has fewer than two lines or a zero, or a line on an account not active in its own book, or is dated outside the book's days or on or before its lock; numbers it in its series (`S` sales documents, `B` bank and payouts, `M` by hand, `IB` opening balances) and year without gaps; and posts what it was posted from once (the same document again returns its entry, unless that was reversed). Nothing posted is changed or deleted: `commerce.ledger_reverse()` puts a mistake right with the signs turned, in the entry's series, on its own day while that is open, once, and never a reversal. A book keeps its store, country, currency and first day, closes once after its last entry and is never deleted; an account with postings keeps its kind. `entryOfDoc()` posts a Kaizena Flow document (`BookingDoc`, the shape Tripletex and Fiken book from): the total on the receivable, each VAT bucket's net on its income account with its standard code (3, 31, 33, 5, 6, 52 for services abroad [U: the accountant's choice]) and each rate's VAT on 2700, 2701 or 2703; a credit note the signs turned; another currency than the book's waits (a rate is step 2's). Where the store books in Tripletex, its own accounts are used (`postingOfTripletex()`), so the comparison is account by account. `ledgerTrialBalance()` reads each account's balance before a period, its debits and credits, and after, and the result. The ledger's audit entries are `work.ledger_*` (the owner's own bookkeeping, D122), ids only. Tests: `src/lib/ledger.test.ts`, `src/db/ledger.test.ts` (every rule against Postgres), `src/server/ledger.int.test.ts`. **Step 2a, documents posted as they are issued (built).** The dispatcher's `ledger` job (`runLedgerPosting()`, 40 seconds) posts, for each store's books open or closed in the last 60 days, the documents issued in their days that have no entry: the same set Tripletex books (Work's sent invoices, not imported ones, and credit notes; the shop's invoices and credit notes), read by the one loader both syncs use (`loadDocument()`), the oldest first. One with an entry, even one a person reversed, is done. One that cannot be posted as it is waits with why (`commerce.ledger_waiting`: another currency, a VAT bucket with no account, totals that do not add up, a locked day) and is tried again a day after it was last tried; the books' screen will list them. Before posting, a standard account the store's posting needs and its chart lacks is added. Tests: `src/server/ledger-posting.int.test.ts` (a Work invoice posted once, one in euro waiting and tried again a day later, a reversed one left be, a shop order's invoice by the job). **Step 3, the screen (built).** Settings → Books (`/settings/books`, in the Advanced sidebar under Store; words a server-only area, `books`): before the books open, the owner chooses the day they start (by default the day Tripletex started booking, else the first of this month) and *Open the books*, which posts the documents of their days at once; then the legal entity and its number, the day the books start and the day they are locked through, what waits and why, the trial balance of any days (this year by default) with each account's balance before, its debits and credits and its balance after, the totals and the period's result, and *Lock* through a day (the owner's; moving it back is audited). Members who may read settings see it. In the admin's map, which the AI manager reads, it was first offered where the owner keeps Work (`needs: "work"`), so the manager's fixed drawing and its recorded eval stayed as they were; on 7 November 2026 it is offered to every store (a shop's invoices are posted too), with the reports and payments in its description, the manager's prompt drawn anew and the eval recorded again on Platform → AI. E2e: `e2e/signed-in/books.spec.ts`. **Step 2b, a document in another currency (built).** It is posted in the book's currency at the rate it was issued at (`fx_rate`, as the document froze it), each line converted and rounded and the VAT lines made to add up to the VAT the document reported in the book's currency (`vat_home_minor`, the rounding on the largest), the receivable their sum; a shop's document only where its VAT's currency is the book's. A document without a rate still waits. **Step 2c, first part: payments for Work invoices (built, 7 November 2026).** Each row of `work_invoice_payments` received in the book's days is posted once in the bank series (`B`) on its day by `entryOfPayment()`: the money where its method puts it (`PAYMENT_ACCOUNTS`: bank and other 1920, cash 1900, card and Stripe 1579 with the payment provider until its payout reaches the bank, a prepayment 2900) against the receivable the invoice was posted to; money paid back the same with the signs turned. In another currency the receivable is cleared at the invoice's own rate and the money is worth the ECB's rate of its day (`rateOnDay()`, the last published on or before it), the difference an exchange gain on 8060 or a loss on 8160. A reversal (`reverses`) turns the payment's own entry line by line (`entryOfPaymentReversal()`), so a mistake is taken back to the øre, and waits (`original`) until that entry is posted; a payment of an imported invoice is posted too, its receivable being in the opening balance. Tripletex's sync books no payments, so nothing is compared. Tests: `ledger.test.ts` (accounts, signs, gain, loss, reversal), `ledger-posting.int.test.ts` (a payment, its reversal, a card payment, one in euro). **Step 2c, second part: the shop's money and Stripe's payouts (built, 7 November 2026).** A shop's captured payment (not a test one) moves its order's receivable to where the money is (`SHOP_PAYMENT_ACCOUNTS`: Stripe's to 1579 until its payout, one taken by hand to the till 1900 or the bank 1920), on the day staff said it came, else the day its order's invoice was issued, else the day it was made (`SHOP_PAYMENT_DAY`); a refund that moves money (`money`, and `release` of a card amount never captured) turns that back on its day, one to store credit owes it to the customer (2900), and one that moves no money (`transfer` to an exchange order, `void` of an unpaid order) posts nothing, its credit note doing the work. A paid payout (`entryOfPayout()`) is what reached the bank (1920) and what Stripe kept (7770, each line's fee and a fee of its own as a line) against the gross out of the provider's balance (1579), on its arrival day; one whose lines are not read yet waits (`lines`), a manual one is posted at its amount. So a charge, its refund and the payout that settles them leave 1579 at nothing. Only in the book's currency for now (another waits, `currency`); a dispute's money stays on 1579 until disputes are posted. Tests: `ledger.test.ts`, `ledger-posting.int.test.ts` (an order's invoice and card payment by the job, its refund, its credit note and the payout, 1579 back to nothing). **Step 2c, third part: gift cards and store credit spent (built, 7 November 2026).** Where a shop payment's money is, or a refund's goes, is one function for every way of paying (`shopMoneyAccount()`): Stripe's on the provider's balance (1579), one taken by hand in the till or the bank, a gift card's off what cards owe (`GIFT_CARD_ACCOUNT`, 2900, where the invoice's `voucher` line put the card sold), store credit's the same (it is a card, D364), and a refund to store credit owed on 2900; an exchange's payment moves no money and is never due; Mollie, a payment at a venue and one on terms wait (`provider`, said on Settings → Books) instead of being posted to the bank as before, where a card's payment would have gone too (none was in production). So a refund to store credit and the credit spent on a later order leave on 2900 exactly what the card still holds (`ledger-posting.int.test.ts`). A card given by staff (source `staff`) is not posted as it is given yet, so its spending takes 2900 below what was sold until that step. **Step 2c, fourth part: shop money in another currency (built, 7 November 2026).** A shop payment or refund in another currency than the book's clears the receivable at its document's own rate (the order's invoice, a refund's credit note, both carrying the rate into the book's currency for VAT, D157) and puts the money where it is at what it was worth in the book's currency (`shopMoneyRates()`): a Stripe payment at what Stripe settled it for, its payout's line, so it waits (`lines`) until that payout is read; one taken by hand at the ECB's rate of its day; the difference an exchange gain (8060) or loss (8160), `PaymentRates.moneyMinor` in `entryOfPayment()`. A gift card or store credit in another currency still waits (`currency`): what cards owe stays at the rate they were sold at. Tested on a euro order paid by card whose payout settled 25.00 kroner above the invoice's rate: the receivable and the provider's balance both end at nothing. **Step 2c, fifth part: disputes (built, 7 November 2026).** A dispute's money is posted as the paid payout's line shows it (`entryOfDisputeLine()`, source `dispute`, on the line's day): taken back from the provider's balance (a negative line), the order's receivable open again, as the customer has not paid after all; given back when the dispute is won (a positive line), the receivable cleared again. The dispute's fee is the payout's, with its other fees (7770). So a disputed charge, its dispute and the payout leave the provider's balance at nothing; a dispute lost leaves the receivable open, for the owner to write off as a loss with the accountant (not yet a line in *Needs you*). Only in the book's currency for now. Step left of 2c: cards given by staff. **Step 2d: the opening balance read from Tripletex (built, 7 November 2026).** On Settings → Books, while the books have none and Tripletex is connected, the owner presses *Bring in the opening balance*: Tripletex's balance sheet (`GET /balanceSheet`, `readTripletexBalances()` in `src/server/ledger-opening.ts`) is read for the day before the books open, and `openingBalanceOf()` makes the entry: each balance sheet account (classes 1 and 2) at what it held, and when the books open during a year each profit and loss account at what it moved since 1 January, so the year's result goes on; on 1 January the balance as that day began. Tripletex's own trial balance must balance to the øre, else nothing is posted and the owner is told by how much. A result of earlier years never carried to equity there is what is left, and goes on 2050 as a line of its own, said to the owner with the advice to check it with the accountant. An account of Tripletex's own that the chart lacks is added with its name, reporting as the standard account nearest below it (`nearestStandard()`: 1921 as 1920). Posted once in the opening balance's series on the day the books open (source `opening_balance`), audited (`work.ledger_opening_posted`), first in the journal; reversed there, it can be read again. Tests: `ledger.test.ts`, `ledger-opening.int.test.ts` (1 July with the year's sales and costs and a second bank account; posted once; refused when an øre off; read again after a reversal; 1 January with last year's uncarried result on 2050), with the Tripletex stand-in's balance sheet. Fiken's opening balance is left for a store that keeps its books there. **Step 3b, first part: the reports (built, 7 November 2026).** Settings → Books shows, for the same days as the trial balance, the profit and loss (`profitAndLoss()`: NS 4102's classes as `RESULT_GROUPS`, 30–35 sales to 83–84 tax, income and costs both positive, the operating result, net financial items, the result before tax and for the period, which is the trial balance's), the balance sheet on the last day (`balanceSheet()`: fixed and current assets, equity, long- and short-term debt, and the result of every day so far not yet carried to equity as a line of its own, so the two sides agree; a mismatch says so) and VAT by code (`vatByCode()`, `ledgerVatByCode()`: each SAF-T standard code's base from its income and cost lines and its VAT from the 27xx lines, sales and output VAT positive, with the VAT to pay), with the two-month VAT term the last day is in (`vatTermOf()`) one press away. Tests: `ledger.test.ts` (groups, results, a balanced sheet, VAT by code, terms), `ledger-posting.int.test.ts` (VAT by code of two invoices, one in euro), `e2e/signed-in/books.spec.ts`. **Step 3b, second part: entries by hand and the journal (built, 7 November 2026).** The owner posts an entry by hand on Settings → Books (one step away, behind *Post an entry*): its kind (an entry by hand, series `M`, or the opening balance, `IB`; never the series documents are posted in), its day, what it is, and up to eight rows of an account from the chart, a debit or a credit and a VAT code where it has one (`handEntryOf()`: an empty row left out, a row with both or neither said, an amount read as typed in the book's currency with no floating point, then the entry's own rules, balanced to the øre), posted by `ledger_post` as every entry is and kept in the audit log (`work.ledger_entry_posted`). The journal lists the latest 30 entries, newest first, each with its lines, what it was posted from (or *By hand*), and what reversed it or what it reverses; the owner reverses one from there (`reverseLedgerEntry()`, once, on its own day while that is open, else today). Tests: `ledger.test.ts` (rows read, problems by row, series), `ledger-posting.int.test.ts` (an unbalanced entry refused, an opening balance posted, in the journal, reversed once), `e2e/signed-in/books.spec.ts` (posted after a refusal, found in the journal, reversed). Step 3b is done. **Step 4, compared with Tripletex (built).** Each document posted here that the store's Tripletex sync booked there (its row `synced`, with the voucher's id) is read back as the sync reads it (`GET /ledger/voucher/{id}`, its postings' account numbers and amounts) and compared (`compareWithTheirs()`): every account but the VAT group by its amount without VAT, and the VAT as one total (here the VAT accounts' lines, there what Tripletex worked out of each gross amount, which holds whether or not it lists its VAT postings apart). The result is kept (`commerce.ledger_comparisons`: `agrees`, `differs` with each account's two amounts, or `missing` when the voucher is gone); one that does not agree is compared again a day later. The dispatcher's `ledger` job compares after it posts, and Settings → Books says how many agree, differ or are gone, and what differs, by the øre. Reads only from Tripletex. Tests: `src/lib/ledger.test.ts`, `src/server/ledger-compare.int.test.ts` (a document that agrees, one whose voucher was changed in Tripletex by an øre, one whose voucher was deleted). Advisors checked after: INFO only (RLS on, no policy, as every private table). | 2026-11-06 | The plan's next unit on the books track (section 7): the AS's books open on 1 January 2027 and should be kept beside Tripletex from their opening balance. |
| D479 | **The language a visitor sees first, the language switcher, and the currency with the language (`src/lib/language-rule.ts`, `src/lib/language-view.ts`, `src/lib/language-switch.ts`, `LanguageLinks`, `languageSwitchStyle()`).** Asked for by the owner: how a store with several languages decides which one a visitor sees, a language switcher an owner places and shapes, and a currency that can follow the language. **The rule** (`stores.language_rule`, Settings → Languages and currencies, *The language a visitor sees first*, while Several languages is on and the store has more than one): `browser` (`Accept-Language`; `no` and `nn` read Bokmål), `location-browser` (the browser's language where the store has one it asks for, else where they are), `location` (the language of the country the visitor is in, `x-vercel-ip-country`, `COUNTRY_LANGUAGES`) and `own` (each country's own language). **The default** (the owner, 6 November 2026): a store made from now on starts with `browser`; every store made before keeps `own`, as it was, so no live store changes (the migration adds the column with `own` and then makes `browser` its default). A store made from a template does not take the template's rule; a store's copy (D129, `duplicate_store()`) keeps its original's three settings. Under every rule the visitor's own choice comes first: choosing a language in a switcher (the new one or the country menu's) keeps it in `kaizen_lang_{storeId}` for a year, a cookie the store's cookie page declares as necessary (the visitor's own choice of how the store is shown, as light or dark, D99), set only while Several languages is on. **Only the front door decides:** a store in one country sends a visitor at `/` (or `/s/{store}`) on its own address to their language's address (`/en`, `/en-eur`) with a 307 that is private and never cached (`languageAtDoor()`, the proxy); never a crawler, never on a country's or language's own domain, never any other address. A store in several countries keeps its chooser (D338: it suggests, never redirects) and its links lead each country in the language the rule picks there (`firstSlug()`). *Why only the front door:* a link to a page in one language (a search result, an advertisement, a shared link) is the version the visitor asked for, and the Geo-blocking Regulation (EU 2018/302, art. 3(2)) forbids sending a visitor to a version in another language by where they are without their consent; search engines also need each language's addresses to stay put. The settings page says so in a sentence. **The switcher** is the site part *Languages*, now a store's as well as Kaizena Flow's (`SITE_PARTS.languages`, shown while the visitor has more than one language): side by side (the default), one under another or a drop-down list; each language by its name in itself (the default), its short code (`EN`) or no words; with a flag or not (the country its variant names, `flagOf()`: `en-IE` Irish, else where most of its readers are; 33 flags from flag-icons 7.2.3, MIT, in `public/flags/`, Spain's and Croatia's about 16 kB gzipped). Each of the three can differ by screen size (`SiteBlock.switcher`, `langText`, `langFlag` and the same keys in `at`, D179): the page is drawn once with the list and the menu, names, codes and flags, and the part stylesheet shows what each size asks (`languageSwitchStyle()`; a name not shown is still read, so every link keeps its name; no words and no flag is the short code). In the library the video is named *(animation: picture and mask)*, because it is odd to look at by itself. Picture and mask together must fit what every phone's decoder takes (H.264 levels 4 to 4.2: 8,704 blocks of 16 pixels a frame), so `stackedPictureSize()` makes a 1920 × 1080 source 1394 × 784 inside the video; the still is 1600 × 900, so what it rests on is the sharper of the two. A file that cannot be an animation is refused in the owner's words before anything is uploaded: not a WebM; over 200 MB; no see-through background (use the Video component); longer than 20 seconds (use the Video component); too small; a browser that cannot prepare it (Safari and Firefox cannot read a WebM's transparency back: use Chrome or Edge on a computer or an Android phone); unreadable. **What a visitor gets (`AnimationPlayer`):** a canvas with a see-through background, drawn from the video by two small shaders (WebGL), and over it the last frame as a picture with the description. Nothing shows until it starts, as an animation opens on its first frame; it starts when a quarter of it is on the screen, plays without sound or controls, and then the picture is laid over the canvas's last frame and the video is let go, so it rests sharp at any size and holds no decoder. *Play again and again* (Style) keeps it going round instead. The picture is shown at once, and no video is fetched, for visitors who prefer less motion and without scripts (both by the picture's own classes and a `noscript` copy, no script of ours), in a browser that cannot draw it, where the browser will not start it (a phone saving power), and on a line that has not started it in 8 seconds. The player is a lazy view (`lazy/blocks`), so its script comes only to pages that have one. **As a picture otherwise:** a description (the publish check asks for one, as for a picture), an optional link, and under Style its width and position by screen size (`ImageSizeFields`). The description is translated with the page. Copied to another store or saved as a template, its two files go together, and it is left empty where either cannot. Added from the sidebar its settings open, as every component's that is nothing until it is filled. **The logo (`SiteBlock.animation`, `AnimatedLogo`, `AnimatedLogoFields`):** a header's or footer's logo part has the same one button, *Animated logo*. `Brand` (a store's and Kaizena Flow's) then draws the animation in the logo's place, as tall as the logo is (the part's height, else the usual one by screen size) and as wide as its shape makes it, so it must be framed closely on the logo. It plays once a visit: the tab's storage remembers it (`kz-animation:logo:{store}`), and a script in the page itself, right after it (`animationSeenScript()`, the colour mode's way, D99), marks it as seen before anything is drawn, so every later page has the logo at once and never waits for the page's scripts. The site's logo in Settings stays what everything else shows (emails, documents, sharing, the admin). One animation serves light and dark: there is no second one for dark backgrounds. **The admin's words:** every admin screen's first scripts carry the catalogues' English (D533), and the home screen had 234 bytes of room. The animation's words are a server-only area (`animation` in `SERVER_AREAS`, D534's way): English in `src/lib/animation-words.ts`, which comes with the fields, and a page in another language hands them down (`useHandedText("animation")`). The three words the builder itself needs (the component's name, *this animation*, *No animation yet.*) were paid for by saying *Double-click or use the wrench.* once (`emptyHow`, added by `emptyWords()` for the components whose settings open when added) instead of in fifteen `emptyBlock` texts. **Not done, and said to the owner:** it was tested in Chromium here, not on an iPhone; the player uses only what Safari has (H.264 and WebGL). A looping animation has no pause button, as a row's background video has none: a visitor's setting for less motion is the way to stop it (WCAG 2.2.2 would ask for a control on what moves for more than five seconds). The AI manager cannot make an animation. The Video component still shows a see-through WebM on black in Safari and does not yet say to use this component instead. Tests: `animation.test.ts`, `animation-block.test.ts`, `animation-view.test.ts`, `e2e/animation.spec.ts`, `e2e/signed-in/builder-animation.spec.ts`. No migration. |

## Open

### Required before the first sale

These come with selling online in these countries, whatever the platform:
WooCommerce and Shopify need them too.

| # | Item | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Norwegian VAT (MVA) registration | You | Once Norwegian sales pass NOK 50,000 in 12 months. |
| R2 | Decide how EU VAT is collected: register for IOSS, or let the carrier collect from customers on delivery | You (+ accountant) | IOSS is the better customer experience. See above. |
| R3 | Terms of sale, withdrawal information and privacy policy in Norwegian, Swedish and Danish | Claude drafts, you review | Built into Phase 1. |
| R4 | Packaging producer responsibility in each market | You | Check whether your volumes trigger registration in Norway, Sweden and Denmark; record numbers in `commerce.producer_registrations` (per store). |
| R5 | Product-safety contact details per manufacturer, and an EU responsible person where needed | You | The database will not activate a product without them. |
| R6 | Check the standard VAT rates in `commerce.countries` and decide on Stripe Tax for reduced rates (food, books, children's clothing) | You (+ accountant) | Orders show VAT at the standard rate of the shopper's country until then. |
| R7 | Turn on customer receipts in Stripe (Settings → Customer emails → Successful payments) | Each store owner | Optional since D26: Kaizen sends its own order confirmation once Resend is set up; Stripe's receipt is a second copy. |

### Not needed now

| Item | When it becomes relevant |
|---|---|
| Sentry, PostHog, GrowthBook accounts | Optional. Add one when Vercel's built-in tools stop being enough (D13). |
| Cookie-consent review per country | Only if non-essential cookies or pixels are added (D14). |
| Data protection impact assessment | Before the AI assistant launches (Phase 3). |
| Accountant review of the VAT setup | Recommended before launch, not legally required. |
| Data processing agreements with Vercel and Supabase | Account-level; if your team and organisation already have them, this project is covered. |
